pr_title: Fix control point pollution from editor or mod alterations
pr_body:
`ControlPointInfo` is considered to be a mutable component of a `Beatmap`, but nothing is done to ensure it doesn't pollute source beatmaps on copy/convert. This makes a deep cloned copy of `ControlPointInfo` on entering the editor or gameplay (via `EditorBeatmap` and `GameplayBeatmap`).

It also changes relevant components in the editor to access the `EditorBeatmap` instead of the via the `WorkingBeatmap`, which solves multiple issues of editor components not updating on control point / timing changes (the timeline now updates its ticks as expected, yay). In places where there was potential to use the wrong beatmap to access dependencies, I removed/replaced `protected WorkingBeatmap` definitions to avoid developer error in the future.

Closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/11408.

issue_context.title: Changes to beatmap control point lists can persist in beatmap cache
issue_context.body:
Originally spotted in https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/11354, but this is a deeper issue. I don't believe this has been reported yet, quite amazingly?

This affects any mod that might want to change control points to alter gameplay, but also the editor. Reproduction scenario for the latter:

1. Choose map in song select
2. Edit said map
3. Change something very visibly in control points (e.g. set a ridiculous difficulty control point like 5x or something)
4. Quit out without saving
5. Play map
6. Changes to control points will persist in gameplay

We probably want to ensure proper change revert everywhere where this can be changed, i.e. via leasing or something (not sure if supported for `BindableList`?)
comments: on exiting the editor, the (working) beatmap needs to be completely reloaded, bypassing any cache. we can't deal with these scenarios on a per-bindable level because things will just get too complex.

True; that should probably also be the case after exiting gameplay with any mod that implements `IApplicableToBeatmap` (or maybe some sort of new interface?) because those also potentially fiddle with control points (as the PR linked in OP does).
